model: Online broker FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route, net debt held at zero, capital retention charged on revenue growth)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case FY2026-FY2030 revenue CAGR (forward). Historical equity CAGR (24.6%/29.7%) is not a usable forward proxy: it embeds the 2019 IPO, 2021 follow-on/convertible funding and the FY2025 trading-cycle peak.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 24.6% vs revenue 3yr CAGR 39.5% (38% relative gap, >30% threshold): revenue outgrew retained capital through FY2023-FY2025 as the business swung from break-even to a 28% net margin. EPS 3yr CAGR undefined (FY2022 EPS 0.00, FY2023 loss-adjacent). FCF CAGRs are null because reported FCF is client-money flow for a broker (see inputs.notes); the owner series is the net-income-based FCFE, FY2022 -2.3 -> FY2025 171.5, from a loss base so no CAGR is meaningful.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue FY2020 138.5 -> FY2022 225.4 -> FY2025 612.1 (US$m). Equity FY2020 235.7 -> FY2022 447.0 -> FY2025 865.5 -> 887.1 at 30-Jun-2026. TTM revenue to 30-Jun-2026 = 612.06 - 261.33 (H1-25) + 337.15 (H1-26) = 687.9. SBC/revenue fell from 10.1% (FY2018, IPO-era) to 2.55% (FY2025) and 1.94% (H1-2026); SBC is a minor drag here, unlike US tech.

scenario_narratives.base: Tiger Brokers keeps growing funded accounts ~10%/yr and client assets faster, offsetting the sell-only wind-down of mainland clients and a lower-rate interest line; revenue compounds ~9% over FY2026-30 and ~5% thereafter at a steady ~32% pre-tax margin (ex SBC/D&A), with US$1.20 of equity retained per US$1 of revenue growth to fund regulatory capital behind the margin book. Discounted at a 12.5% cost of equity with 3% terminal growth; net debt is zero by construction and corporate cash is treated as regulatory capital, not surplus.
scenario_narratives.bull: Retail participation, HK retail crypto dealing and wealth-management distribution lift growth to the mid-teens for three years and margins back to 35%; incremental capital needs ease to US$1.00 per US$1 of revenue growth and the tax rate holds at 21%.
scenario_narratives.bear: A 2027 stall and 2028 risk-off year compress margins to 18% before a slow recovery to 25%; mainland exit, fee compression and higher capital intensity (US$1.40 per US$1) cap growth at 3-4%, tax at 25%. The resulting value sits close to today's price - the market is pricing roughly this case, plus a China-ADR structural discount.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A broker's value is the equity cash flow left after the capital its margin book and regulators demand, discounted at the cost of equity - not an unlevered FCF stream over client-money noise. Tangible book of US$887m (30-Jun-2026) is roughly US$4.79 per diluted ADS, so at the current price the market pays below book for a business earning a ~18-20% ROE ex the penalty; the model asks what that excess return is worth if it fades with growth, and charges the China/regulatory/cyclical risk once, through the bear flows and a 30% bear weight rather than a stacked discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Trading-volume and rate cyclicality: commissions (44%) and interest income (42%) both fall in a risk-off, easing-cycle year; FY2022 revenue fell 15% and FY2022-23 net income was ~zero

Mainland-China client wind-down after the CSRC settlement removes a historically high-activity cohort over a multi-year window; any further PRC action on data, capital controls or the offshore structure is not priced beyond the bear weight
China-ADR structural discount (HFCAA, geopolitics) can keep the price below intrinsic value indefinitely; the model values flows, not the re-rating

Capital retention is a judgment (US$1.20 per US$1 of incremental revenue); if regulators or margin-book growth demand materially more equity, FCFE and the value fall roughly in proportion to the retention step
Competitive CAC inflation (guided US$450-550 per funded account) and secular take-rate compression against Futu, IBKR, Webull and Robinhood
Margin-lending credit losses in a sharp drawdown (receivables from customers US$2.19bn = 2.5x equity)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 4.00-11.35 (USD per ADS)
data_sources.financials: FY2025 20-F (SEC XBRL companyfacts, filed 2026-04-24) for FY2024-FY2025 revenue, pre-tax income, tax, SBC, D&A, equity; Q1-2026 6-K ex99.1 (filed 2026-06-02) and Q2-2026 6-K ex99.1 (filed 2026-08-26) for the 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet, H1-2026 income statement, SBC reconciliation, ADS ratio and share counts; TIGR_Metrics.csv for the FY2017-FY2025 history
data_sources.qualitative: TIGR_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): business mix, CSRC settlement, Q2-2026 call commentary (Q3 trading slightly below Q2, CAC US$450-550, client assets +high single digit QoQ); FUTU peer valuation (FUTU_DCF.json) for model consistency

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 20-F (filed 2026-04-24) non-GAAP reconciliation, US$15.6m; H1-2026 US$6.54m (Q1 3.05 + Q2 3.48) from the 6-K ex99.1 non-GAAP reconciliation tables
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:00Z regular close (Friday; valuation written Saturday 2026-10-04, no later print exists)
inputs.share_count_basis: ADS-equivalent, millions. 1 ADS = 15 Class A ordinary shares (stated in every quarterly release). Q2-2026 weighted-average diluted ADS used for non-GAAP EPS = 185,044,751 (6-K ex99.1, 26-Aug-2026); GAAP diluted 2,745,917,801 ordinary = 183.06m ADS; period-end basic 2,697,680,337 ordinary = 179.85m ADS. The higher non-GAAP diluted count is used (conservative). The CSV SharesOutstanding column (2,807.7m for FY2025) is the diluted weighted-average ORDINARY share count, not ADSs - dividing the ADS price by it would understate value 15x. Held flat: SBC is expensed in the flows, and the US$50m 12-month buyback approved 1-Jun-2026 (~US$5m executed by 26-Aug-2026) more than funds any residual creep.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 12.5% applied to equity flows. Statements and the bulk of the flows are USD (HKD/SGD-pegged or USD-denominated client balances), so the USD risk-free basis applies: 10y UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.5 x 5.5% ERP = 12.5%. One point above the FUTU peer build (11.5%) for smaller scale, thinner capital base and a shorter profitable history. Single rate across all three scenarios: cyclicality, the mainland wind-down and China-ADR structural risk are charged in the bear flows and the bear-tilted weights, not stacked in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases immaterial (ROU assets US$8.6m, lease liabilities US$8.2m at 30-Jun-2026 against US$887m equity); lease cost sits inside the occupancy line and therefore inside the pre-tax margin. Nothing deducted from net debt (held at zero). One treatment, in the flows.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are negative US$0.25m and redeemable NCI US$5.3m; attributable net income differs from consolidated by <US$0.3m/yr. Flows are consolidated; no NCI deduction (immaterial, stated).
inputs.notes: MODEL: UP Fintech is an online securities broker-dealer: it carries a US$2.19bn margin-financing book (receivables from customers), US$4.16bn of segregated client cash and US$6.24bn of payables to customers on a US$9.75bn balance sheet against US$0.89bn of equity (30-Jun-2026). Per dcf-methods routing this is bank/broker-like (closest row: non-bank deposit taker / residual income on tangible book). Reported OCF/FCF is client-money noise (FY2023 -US$9m, FY2024 +US$826m, FY2025 +US$1,311m on net income of 33/61/171) and borrowings/payables are operating funding, so an unlevered owner-FCF DCF is meaningless. Valued as FCFE at the cost of equity on the engine route, exactly as the FUTU peer and the house approach for financials (NAB.AX, BMO, STT, USB): revenue x pre-tax margin before SBC and D&A ('ebitda_margin_path') -> SBC -> cash tax = net income; capital retention charged through wc_capture_pct as US$1.20 of retained equity per US$1 of incremental revenue in the base case (equity/TTM revenue 1.29x at 30-Jun-2026; margin receivables are 2.5x equity and regulatory liquid-capital rules in HK/SG/US/NZ/AU scale with the margin book), US$1.00 bull, US$1.40 bear. A falling revenue year therefore releases capital, which is why the bear path is kept to a mild -5% rather than a deep trough. net_debt = 0: payables to customers, payables to brokers and the US$53m convertible bond are operating funding; corporate cash (US$542m) and financial instruments (US$126m) are regulatory capital supporting the margin book and are NOT credited as surplus - this also absorbs the ~US$60m CSRC penalty accrued at 30-Jun-2026 (accrued expenses rose US$74m in H1) which is a claim on that cash. interest_income is 0 because interest on margin loans and client cash is operating revenue (42% of FY2025 revenue) - it must not be deducted. last_fcf (168.9) is FY2025 FCFE before growth retention: net income 171.5 + D&A 2.9 - capex 5.5; reported_fcf (184.5) is the same with SBC 15.6 added back (street basis). The CSV FreeCashFlow column (1,311) is not used. ONE-OFF: the Q1-2026 'Others, net' of -US$64.1m carries the RMB411m (~US$59.7m) CSRC Beijing Bureau penalty plus confiscated gains (settled 22-May-2026, recognised in Q1); it is excluded from the starting margin (H1-2026 pre-tax ex-penalty ~US$100m = 29.6% of revenue; +SBC +D&A = ~32% 'EBITDA' margin, versus 36.9% in FY2025 and 24% in FY2024). Tax: FY2025 effective rate 17.3% was the low point (FY2024 25.0%, H1-2026 ex-penalty ~25%); base uses 23%. ADS/ADR: Cayman holdco, Nasdaq ADS, foreign private issuer; HFCAA/delisting narrative is part of the structural discount carried by the bear weight.

bear.narrative: H2-2026 trading cools faster than guided (FY +11%), 2027 flat as mainland clients exit and Fed cuts bite the interest line, 2028 a 2022-style risk-off year (-5% revenue, FY2022 was -15%) with sticky compensation/marketing taking the pre-tax margin to 18%, then a slow recovery to a 25% margin - a permanently more competitive, lower-rate brokerage with heavier capital needs (US$1.40 per US$1 of revenue growth) and a 25% tax rate.

base.growth_note: FY2026 +14% = H1 actual 337.1 + H2 ~360 (Q3 guided 'slightly below Q2' trading pace, interest income still compounding on a US$7.4bn margin book +29% YoY; H2-2025 base was 350.7). FY2027-28 held to 8-9% because the CSRC settlement forces a multi-year sell-only wind-down of mainland clients (~10% of client assets at Dec-2025) that nets ~4-5 points a year off underlying low-teens growth; Fed easing compresses the 42% interest-income stream. Fade to 3% nominal by year 10.
base.margin_note: 32.5% pre-tax/pre-SBC/pre-D&A margin = H1-2026 run-rate ex the CSRC penalty (Q1 32.2%, Q2 32.3%). Flat to 32%: operating leverage on communication/market-data and clearing offsets CAC guided up to US$450-550 per funded account and secular take-rate compression. FY2025's 36.9% is treated as a cycle peak, not a base.
base.tax_note: 23% blends Singapore 17%, HK 16.5%, US 21%, NZ 28%, AU 30% and non-deductible items; FY2024 25.0%, FY2025 17.3%, H1-2026 ex-penalty ~25%.
base.retention_note: wc_capture_pct -120 = US$1.20 of equity retained per US$1 of incremental revenue, holding equity/revenue near 1.2-1.3x (1.29x at 30-Jun-2026). FY2026 FCFE ~US$57m on ~US$160m net income (35% payout) - consistent with no dividend and a US$50m buyback.

bull.narrative: Sustained retail risk appetite, HK virtual-asset dealing extended to retail, wealth-management/IPO 'other revenue' keeps compounding at 60%+, international (HK/SG/AU/NZ/US) inflows more than replace the mainland wind-down, margins recover toward the FY2025 level, retention eases to US$1.00 per US$1 of revenue growth as the capital base matures.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% house default and matched to the FUTU peer build: the analysis rates the business highly cyclical and rate-sensitive, H1-2026 sits on record trading volumes, a sell-only wind-down of mainland clients is now mandated, and the stock carries China-ADR (HFCAA/geopolitical) tail risk that the flows cannot capture. Base 50% for the international-diversification path management is visibly executing (mainland ~10% of client assets, HK/SG/AU/NZ/US growing, Q2-2026 record revenue). Bull cut to 20% because it needs a sustained bull market, retail crypto approval and benign rates simultaneously. The CSRC settlement (May-2026) is a quantified, booked one-off and is not re-charged here.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
